newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba member Jochimsen won't rule out rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Buba member Jochimsen won't rule out rate cut.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen has said he would not rule out another reduction in Bundesbank interest rates in the present economic cycle but added that he did not see one.
He told reporters at a dinner on Wednesday evening that acceleration in M3 money supply growth in May was not good but not dramatic either.
"I see with a certain amount of concern that price pressures are emerging from abroad and in raw materials," Jochimsen said.
But he added that price increases were not accelerating.
"The increase in M3 growth is not nice but it's not dramatic," Jochimsen said. "I don't rule out a further interest rate cut but I don't see it."

M3 money supply growth in May accelerated to 7.0 percent from 6.7 percent in April, surprising financial markets which had expected the Bundesbank's key policy indicator to enter its target growth zone for 1997 of 3.5 percent to 6.5 percent.
Jochimsen is president of the state central bank of North Rhine-Westphalia.
